relations.myth: Making of the Fifth Sun and moon
relations.note: They perform penance and enter the fire as rival candidates for cosmic illumination.
Nanahuatzin rises first as the sun; Tecciztecatl follows with equal brilliance.

relations.myth: Variant creation of the Fifth Sun
relations.note: The poor solar candidate contrasts with the second luminary, whose identity differs from Sahagún.

relations.myth: Variant creation of the second luminary
relations.note: This named second luminary occupies Tecciztecatl’s role in a related textual variant.
Quetzalcoatl predicts an eastern emergence before Tecciztecatl rises after Nanahuatzin.

relations.myth: Setting the sun and moon in motion
relations.note: Ehecatl kills or drives the gods’ deaths, then moves the luminaries.
Xiuhtecuhtli directs Nanahuatzin toward the fire where the second luminary also transforms.
Xolotl evades divine death through transformations after Tecciztecatl has become the moon.
Later systematization pairs Tonatiuh as the present sun with Tecciztecatl as moon.
